summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are short 'X doesn't see/hear, it only senses Y' myth-busting videos about robots and clap switches (Gyro robot, Clap Switch, Line Follower). Newer videos from mid-November dropped to 100-300 views, and generic 'How does X work? 🤔' titles get almost nothing.
winningPattern: Robot or Arduino-module subject (gyro, clap switch, IR, mic, DHT11) + a myth-flip hook in Hinglish ('Doesn't see/hear, only senses...' or 'Without X the robot falls') + a curiosity emoji + #shorts, posted mainly on Instagram Reels. Visible, demo-able hardware that people can build beats household explainers like malls, lifts and taps. Very short 'why' questions also drive saves and shares.
doMore: Lead with a myth-flip hook: 'Robot X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' on robots and Arduino modules
Make follow-ups of the top hits: gyro/balancing robot, clap switch variants, line follower, mic vs speaker
Make each video about one maker-friendly module with a visible demo or a before/after failure moment
End with a build-it or save-it line, since saves and shares signal strong interest ('Save this for your project')
Post at the early-to-mid pace that earned 1,000+ views and reuse the same hook style in titles and on-screen text
stopDoing: Generic 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on household devices like malls, taps and lifts
Spending effort on YouTube-only uploads or English videos until the Hindi hook style is working there too
Niche appliance topics (geyser, chimney, TDS meter, soil sensor) that earned under 400 views
